## I APPLICATION OF THIS PART

## Scope and interpretation

## 80.1

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (1) This Part contains rules about–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (a) TPIM proceedings in the High Court, and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (b) appeals to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in such proceedings. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (2) In the case of proceedings brought by virtue of section 17(2) of the Act, the rules in this Part shall apply with any modification the court considers necessary. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (3) In this Part –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (a) ‘the Act’ means the Terrorism, Prevention and Investigation Measures Act 2011;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (b) ‘closed material’ means any relevant material that the Secretary of State objects to disclosing to a relevant party on the grounds that it is contrary to the public interest;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (c) ‘extension notice’ means a notice issued under section 5(2) of the Act, extending a TPIM notice;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (d) ‘legal representative’ is to be construed in accordance with paragraph 4(4)(b) of Schedule 4 to the Act;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (e) ‘measures’ means terrorism prevention and investigation measures (which has the same meaning as in section 2 of the Act);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (f) ‘open material’ means any relevant material that the Secretary of State does not object to disclosing to a relevant party on the grounds that it is contrary to the public interest;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (g) ‘relevant material’ means the material described in paragraph 3(1)(a) to (c) of Schedule 4 to the Act;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (h) ‘relevant party’ means any party to the proceedings other than the Secretary of State;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (i) ‘revival notice’ means a notice issued under section 13(6) of the Act, reviving a TPIM notice;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (j) ‘special advocate’ means a person appointed under paragraph 10(1) of Schedule 4 to the Act;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (k) ‘TPIM notice’ has the same meaning as in section 2(1) of the Act;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (l) ‘TPIM proceedings’ has the same meaning as in section 30(1) of the Act;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (m) ‘TPIM subject’ means an individual on whom the Secretary of State has imposed, or is proposing to impose, measures by means of a TPIM notice;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (n) ‘variation notice’ means a notice issued under section 12(1)(c) of the Act, varying the TPIM notice without the individual’s consent. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.1] (4) For the purposes of this Part, disclosure is contrary to the public interest if it is made contrary to the interests of national security, the international relations of the United Kingdom or the detection and prevention of crime, or in any other circumstances where disclosure is likely to harm the public interest. ## Modification to the overriding objective

## 80.2

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.2] (1) Where this Part applies, the overriding objective in Part 1, and so far as relevant any other rule, must be read and given effect in a way which is compatible with the duty set out in paragraph (2). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.2] (2) The court must ensure that information is not disclosed contrary to the public interest. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.2] (3) Subject to paragraph (2), the court must satisfy itself that the material available to it enables it properly to determine proceedings. ## II PERMISSION APPLICATIONS, REFERENCES AND APPEALS TO THE HIGH COURT RELATING TO TPIM NOTICES

## Scope of this section

## 80.3

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.3] This section contains rules about–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.3] (a) applications under section 6(1)(b) of the Act (application for permission to impose measures);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.3] (b) references under paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2 to the Act (reference of the imposition of measures imposed without permission); and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.3] (c) appeals to the High Court under section 16 of the Act (appeals relating to a TPIM notice). ## Application for permission to impose measures

## 80.4

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.4] An application under section 6(1)(b) of the Act for permission to impose measures must be made by the Secretary of State filing with the court –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.4] (a) a statement of reasons to support the application;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.4] (b) any relevant material of which the Secretary of State is aware at that stage;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.4] (c) any written submissions; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.4] (d) the proposed TPIM notice. ## Reference of measures imposed without permission

## 80.5

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.5] A reference under paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2 to the Act of the imposition of measures imposed without permission is made by the Secretary of State filing with the court –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.5] (a) a statement of reasons for imposing measures and for imposing the measures specified in the TPIM notice;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.5] (b) any relevant material of which the Secretary of State is aware at that stage;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.5] (c) any written submissions; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.5] (d) the TPIM notice. ## Directions for hearing on an application for permission or on a reference

## 80.6

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (1) If the court gives permission on an application under section 6(1)(b) of the Act or confirms a TPIM notice on a reference under paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2 to the Act, the court must give directions for a directions hearing at which the TPIM subject, the TPIM subject’s legal representative, the special advocate (if one has been appointed) and the Secretary of State’s legal representative may be present. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (2) In a case where permission is given (following an application under section 6(1)(b) of the Act), the date to be fixed for the directions hearing must, unless the court otherwise directs, be no later than 7 days after the date on which the TPIM notice is served on the TPIM subject. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (3) In a case where the TPIM notice is confirmed (following a reference under paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2 to the Act), the date to be fixed for the directions hearing must, unless the court otherwise directs, be no later than 7 days after the date on which the court confirms the TPIM notice. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (4) At the directions hearing, the court must give directions –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (a) for a review hearing under section 9(1) of the Act; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (b) specifying a date and time by which the parties and special advocate must file and serve any written evidence or written submissions in accordance with rule 80.26. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (5) When giving directions under paragraph (4), the court must have regard to the need to expedite the review hearing. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.6] (Rules 80.24 and 80.25 will apply where any closed material is filed by the Secretary of State). ## Appeals under section 16 of the Act

## 80.7

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.7] Rules 80.8 to 80.11 apply to an appeal under section 16 of the Act (appeals relating to a TPIM notice). ## Modification of Part 52 (appeals)

## 80.8

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal under section 16 of the Act, subject to –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (a) rules 52.3, 52.4 and 52.6;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (b) the rules in section IV of this Part; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (c) paragraphs (2) and (3). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (2) The following rules do not apply to appeals under section 16 of the Act –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (a) rule 52.3, 52.4 and 52.6 (permission);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (b) rule 52.12 (appellant’s notice);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (c) rule 52.13 (respondent’s notice); and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (d) rule 52.21 (hearing of appeals). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.8] (3) Rule 52.2 (all parties to comply with Practice Directions 52A to 52E apply, but the parties shall not be required to comply with paragraphs 5.1 to 5.3 of Practice Direction 52A and paragraphs 6.3 to 6.6 of Practice Direction 52B. ## Notice of appeal

## 80.9

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (1) The TPIM subject must give notice of appeal by –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (a) filing a notice of appeal with the court; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (b) serving a copy of that notice and any accompanying documents on the Secretary of State. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (2) The notice of appeal must–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (a) set out the grounds of the appeal; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (b) state the name and address of –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (i) the TPIM subject, and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (ii) the TPIM subject’s legal representative (if any). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (3) A notice of appeal may include an application under rule 80.15 for an order requiring anonymity for the TPIM subject. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (4) The notice of appeal must be filed with a copy of the TPIM notice imposing measures on the TPIM subject and (as relevant) –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (a) a copy of the extension notice, revival notice or variation notice that is the subject of the appeal;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (b) a copy of the application to the Secretary of State –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (i) for permission in connection with a measure specified in the TPIM notice,

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (ii) for the revocation of the TPIM notice, or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (iii) for the variation of a measure specified in the TPIM notice;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (c) a copy of the Secretary of State’s decision on such an application. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.9] (Attention is drawn to rule 80.14(1) relating to the address for issuing proceedings in the High Court). ## Time limit for appealing

## 80.10

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.10] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), the TPIM subject must give notice of appeal no later than 28 days after receiving–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.10] (a) the extension notice, revival notice or variation notice that is the subject of the appeal; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.10] (b) notice of the Secretary of State’s decision on an application for permission in connection with a measure specified in the TPIM notice, for the revocation of the TPIM notice or for the variation of a measure specified in the TPIM notice. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.10] (2) In a case where the Secretary of State has failed to determine an application for permission in connection with a measure specified in the TPIM notice, for the revocation of the TPIM notice or for the variation of a measure specified in the TPIM notice, the TPIM subject must file the notice of appeal –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.10] (a) no earlier than 28 days, and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.10] (b) no later than 42 days,

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.10] after the date on which the Secretary of State received the application. ## Secretary of State’s reply

## 80.11

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.11] If the Secretary of State wishes to oppose an appeal, the Secretary of State must, no later than 14 days after being served with the notice of appeal –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.11] (a) file with the court–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.11] (i) any relevant material of which the Secretary of State is aware at that stage; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.11] (ii) any written submissions; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.11] (b) serve on the TPIM subject any open material. ## III APPEALS TO THE COURT OF APPEAL

## Modification of Part 52 (appeals)

## 80.12

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in TPIM proceedings, subject to –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (a) rule 80.2;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (b) the rules in section IV of this Part; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (c) paragraphs (2) and (3). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (2) The following rules do not apply to appeals to the Court of Appeal –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (a) rule 52.12(1) (appellant’s notice); and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (b) rule 52.13 (respondent’s notice), but

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] the provisions of rules 80.9 and 80.11 shall apply with appropriate modifications. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.12] (3) Rule 52.2 (all parties to comply with Practice Directions 52A to 52E apply, but the parties shall not be required to comply with paragraphs 6.3 to 6.6 of Practice Direction 52B and paragraph 28 of Practice Direction 52C. ## IV GENERAL PROVISIONS

## Scope of this section

## 80.13

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.13] This section applies to –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.13] (a) TPIM proceedings in the High Court; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.13] (b) appeals to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in such proceedings. ## Address for filing proceedings

## 80.14

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.14] (1) Any TPIM proceedings must be filed at the Administrative Court Office, Room C315, Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London, WC2A 2LL. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.14] (2) Any appeals to the Court of Appeal against an order of the High Court in such proceedings must be filed at the Civil Appeals Office, Room E307, Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London, WC2A 2LL. ## Applications for anonymity

## 80.15

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.15] (1) The TPIM subject or the Secretary of State may apply for an order requiring anonymity for the TPIM subject. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.15] (2) An application under paragraph (1) may be made at any time, irrespective of whether any TPIM proceedings have been commenced. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.15] (3) An application may be made without notice to the other party. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.15] (4) The reference in this rule to an order requiring anonymity for the TPIM subject is to be construed in accordance with paragraph 6(3) of Schedule 4 to the Act. ## Notification of hearing

## 80.16

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.16] Unless the court directs otherwise, it will serve notice of the date, time and place fixed for any hearing on–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.16] (a) every party, whether or not entitled to attend that hearing; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.16] (b) if one has been appointed for the purposes of the hearing, the special advocate or those instructing the special advocate. ## Hearings

## 80.17

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (1) The following proceedings must be determined at a hearing –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (a) a review hearing under section 9(1) of the Act (review hearing);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (b) an appeal under section 16 of the Act (appeals relating to a TPIM notice);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (c) an appeal to the Court of Appeal from an order of the High Court made in the proceedings mentioned in sub-paragraph (a) or (b) above; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (d) a hearing under rule 80.25(2) (consideration of the Secretary of State’s objection or application). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (2) Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply where the court discontinues the review hearing in accordance with section 9(3) of the Act. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (3) Paragraph (1)(b) does not apply where –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (a) the appeal is withdrawn by the TPIM subject;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (b) the Secretary of State consents to the appeal being allowed; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (c) the TPIM subject is outside the United Kingdom or it is impracticable to give the TPIM subject notice of a hearing and, in either case, the TPIM subject is unrepresented. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (4) Paragraph (1)(c) does not apply where –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (a) the Court of Appeal grants a request by the appellant to dismiss the appeal;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (b) the Court of Appeal allows the appeal with consent; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.17] (c) the Court of Appeal strikes out the appeal. ## Hearings in private

## 80.18

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.18] (1) If the court considers it necessary for any relevant party and any relevant party’s legal representative to be excluded from a hearing or part of a hearing in order to secure that information is not disclosed contrary to the public interest, it must–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.18] (a) direct accordingly; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.18] (b) conduct the hearing, or that part of it from which the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative are excluded, in private. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.18] (2) The court may conduct a hearing or part of a hearing in private for any other good reason. ## Appointment of a special advocate

## 80.19

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary of State must immediately give notice of the proceedings to the Attorney General (who, under paragraph 10(1) of Schedule 4 to the Act, has the power to appoint a special advocate) on –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (a) making an application under section 6(1)(b) of the Act (application for permission to impose measures);

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (b) making a reference under paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2 to the Act (reference of the imposition of measures imposed without permission); or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (c) being served with a copy of any application, claim or notice of appeal in proceedings to which this Part applies. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (2) Paragraph (1) applies unless–

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (a) the Secretary of State does not intend to –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (i) oppose the application, claim or appeal; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (ii) withhold closed material from a relevant party; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (b) a special advocate has already been appointed to represent the interests of the relevant party in the proceedings and that special advocate is not prevented from communicating with that party by virtue of rule 80.21. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.19] (3) Where any proceedings to which this Part applies are pending but no special advocate has been appointed, a relevant party or the Secretary of State may request the Attorney General appoints a special advocate. ## Functions of a special advocate

## 80.20

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.20] The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a relevant party by –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.20] (a) making submissions to the court at any hearing or part of a hearing from which the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative are excluded;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.20] (b) adducing evidence and cross-examining witnesses at any such hearing or part of a hearing; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.20] (c) making written submissions to the court. ## Special advocate: communicating about proceedings

## 80.21

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (1) The special advocate may communicate with the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative at any time before the Secretary of State serves closed material on the special advocate. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (2) After the Secretary of State serves closed material on the special advocate, the special advocate must not communicate with any person about any matter connected with the proceedings, except in accordance with paragraph (3) or (6)(b) or with a direction of the court pursuant to a request under paragraph (4). [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (3) The special advocate may, without directions from the court, communicate about the proceedings with –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (a) the court;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (b) the Secretary of State or any person acting for the Secretary of State;

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (c) the Attorney General or any person acting for the Attorney General; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (d) any other person, except the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative, with whom it is necessary for administrative purposes for the special advocate to communicate about matters not connected with the substance of the proceedings. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (4) The special advocate may request directions from the court authorising him or her to communicate with the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative or with any other person. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (5) Where the special advocate makes a request for directions under paragraph (4) –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (a) the court must notify the Secretary of State of the request; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (b) the Secretary of State must, within a period specified by the court, file with the court and serve on the special advocate notice of any objection which the Secretary of State has to the proposed communication, or to the form in which it is proposed to be made. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (6) Paragraph (2) does not prohibit the relevant party from communicating with the special advocate after the Secretary of State has served closed material on the special advocate, but –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (a) the relevant party may only communicate with the special advocate through the relevant party’s legal representative in writing; and

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.21] (b) the special advocate must not reply to the communication other than in accordance with directions of the court, except that the special advocate may without such directions send a written acknowledgment of receipt to the relevant party’s legal representative. ## Modification of the general rules of evidence and disclosure

## 80.22

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (1) Part 31 (disclosure and inspection of documents), Part 32 (evidence) and Part 33 (miscellaneous rules about evidence) do not apply to any proceedings to which this Part applies. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (2) Subject to the other rules in this Part, the evidence of a witness may be given either –

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (a) orally before the court; or

[PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (b) in writing, in which case it shall be given in such manner and at such time as the court directs. [PART 80 – Proceedings under the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation > 80.22] (3) The court may also receive evidence in documentary or any other form.
